newsitem.title: USA: NYS watchdog says NYC must find money for tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: NYS watchdog says NYC must find money for tax cuts.

text.p: New York State's Comptroller, in a scathing assessment of parts of the Giuliani Administration's proposed budget for fiscal 1998, said the mayor needed a plan to pay for $250 million of tax cuts.

"The city is acting like the worker who blows Friday's paycheck that night; reality hits the following week when it comes time to pay for basics, like breakfast, lunch and dinner. Tax cuts need to make sense and you need to have a plan to pay for them," said H. Carl McCall in prepared remarks.

McCall, whose report came on the heels of one issued by the City Comptroller, Alan Hevesi, articulated some of the same criticisms about the city's reliance on risky, one-shot maneuvers, saying they added up to about $1.4 billion in fiscal 1998. Still, this was at the low-end of the $1.4 billion to $2.11 billion range identified by Hevesi.

The state official faulted assertions by Mayor Rudolph Guiliani, who has repeatedly said that one of the reasons New York City has been able to attract tourists and conventions back to the city was his Administration's decision to cut hotel occupancy taxes.

"There are unsubstantiated claims in the city's tax cut strategy," McCall said, in his report. "A case in point is the hotel tax, which the city says has stimulated economic growth. The fact is, occupancy rates were way up before the tax cut, and room prices have been steadily growing, even as the taxes were reduced."
Giuliani also has attributed the recent boom in the city's tourism business to his Administration's notable success in reducing crime rates.
